basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma '« Filii autem Javan Elisa et Tarcis, Cethim et Dodanim. De Ionibus, id est, Graecis'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: « Filii autem Javan Elisa et Tarcis, Cethim et Dodanim. De Ionibus, id est, Graecis nascuntur Elisae, qui vocantur Elides, unde et quinta lingua Graeciae Eolis appellatur, quam illi penten dialecton vocant. Tharses Josephus Cilicas arbitratur, Thar aspirationis litteram vitiose a posteris in Tar dicens fuisse corruptam; unde et metropolis eorum civitas Tarsis appelatur, Paulo apostolo gloriosa. (Nonnulli Tharsis unde aurum Salomoni deferebatur Indiae putant esse regionem.) Cethim Cethi a quibus usque hodie urbs Cyptotium nominatur. Dodanim Rhodii, melius enim legitur Rodanim, sive Rodim, ut septuaginta Interpretes transtulerunt, » et in libro Hebraeorum nominum etiam noster interpres posuit. Similitudo enim litterarum Daleth et Res hunc apud Hebraeos saepe facit errorem, ut alia legatur pro alia. Est autem Rhodus Cycladarum maxima, et in Ionio mari quondam urbs potentissima, navalique certamine gloriosa, et propter tutissimum portum mercatorum omnium receptaculum
